title: 'Digital Arrest' Scams — Fake Police, CBI, ED and Customs Video Calls
publisher: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
text: In a 'digital arrest' scam, fraudsters call or video-call the victim pretending to be police, CBI, Enforcement Directorate (ED), Narcotics Control Bureau, customs, TRAI or a judge. They claim the victim's Aadhaar, SIM or bank account is linked to a crime — often a parcel containing drugs, fake passports or contraband, or money laundering — and say the victim is under 'digital arrest'. Victims are kept on a Skype, WhatsApp or other video call for hours or days, told not to speak to anyone, shown fake documents, uniforms and police-station backdrops, and pressured to transfer money to 'verify' their funds or settle the case. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has advised that police, CBI, ED, customs and other agencies do not arrest or interrogate people over video calls, and that there is no such thing as a 'digital arrest' under Indian law. If you receive such a call: do not panic, disconnect, do not share personal or bank details, do not transfer any money, and report it immediately on the national cybercrime helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in. Fraud calls can also be reported on the Sanchar Saathi portal (Chakshu).
